CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Badung Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Badung.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Badung Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a Woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences suffering and/or hardship as a result of Violence and/or threat of Violence.
12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can perform their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
14. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally.
15. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence from the Region to their Region of origin.
16. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
17. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or Victims of acts of Violence.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and Child Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and Legal Aid.
19. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Child Victims of Violence aims to:
a. prevent all forms of Violence against Women and Children;
b. protect Women and provide services to Women and Child Victims of Violence; and
c. empower Women and Child Victims of Violence.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, Violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for Victims of Violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Badung Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children Victims of Violence particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Badung Regency.

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 11

1. To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
2. The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
3. Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Work Units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.
4. Monitoring shall be conducted from the planning stage to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence for the current year.

CHAPTER XI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 16

1. In providing Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, the community may:
a. establish family partners at the sub-district/village level by the community;
b. conduct independent socialization of the rights of Women and Children;
c. provide first aid to Victims; and
d. report to the competent authorities if Violence against Victims occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 15

1. The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision over the implementation of MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes providing implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of services for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 14

Funding for the provision of Protection for Women and Children from acts of Violence shall be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 12

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.
3. The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

REGENT OF BADUNG

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BADUNG REGENCY

NUMBER 15 YEAR 2013 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

CHAPTER VIII

REPORTING

Article 13

1. The Regent is responsible for preparing a report on the implementation of MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region to the Governor with a copy submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.
2. The reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.

CHAPTER XII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 17

In the event that the IPU as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (1) has not been established, the existing P2TP2A shall continue to carry out the duties and functions of integrated services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Badung Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Badung.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Badung Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a Woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences suffering and/or hardship as a result of Violence and/or threat of Violence.
12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can perform their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
14. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally.
15. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence from the Region to their Region of origin.
16. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
17. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or Victims of acts of Violence.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and Child Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and Legal Aid.
19. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Child Victims of Violence aims to:
a. prevent all forms of Violence against Women and Children;
b. protect Women and provide services to Women and Child Victims of Violence; and
c. empower Women and Child Victims of Violence.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, Violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for Victims of Violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Badung Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children Victims of Violence particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Badung Regency.

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 11

1. To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
2. The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
3. Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Work Units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.
4. Monitoring shall be conducted from the planning stage to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence for the current year.

CHAPTER XI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 16

1. In providing Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, the community may:
a. establish family partners at the sub-district/village level by the community;
b. conduct independent socialization of the rights of Women and Children;
c. provide first aid to Victims; and
d. report to the competent authorities if Violence against Victims occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 14

Funding for the provision of Protection for Women and Children from acts of Violence shall be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

REGENT OF BADUNG

Article 12

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.
3. The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 15

1. The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision over the implementation of MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes providing implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of services for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

Article 11

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, Violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for Victims of Violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Badung Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Badung Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Badung.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Badung Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a Woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences suffering and/or hardship as a result of Violence and/or threat of Violence.
12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can perform their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
14. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally.
15. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence from the Region to their Region of origin.
16. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
17. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or Victims of acts of Violence.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and Child Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and Legal Aid.
19. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, Violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for Victims of Violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Badung Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children Victims of Violence particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Badung Regency.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

REGENT OF BADUNG

Article 3

Protection of Women and Child Victims of Violence aims to:
a. prevent all forms of Violence against Women and Children;
b. protect Women and provide services to Women and Child Victims of Violence; and
c. empower Women and Child Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER XIII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 18

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by its placement in the Regional Gazette of Badung Regency.

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 11

1. To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
2. The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
3. Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Work Units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.
4. Monitoring shall be conducted from the planning stage to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence for the current year.

CHAPTER XI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 16

1. In providing Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, the community may:
a. establish family partners at the sub-district/village level by the community;
b. conduct independent socialization of the rights of Women and Children;
c. provide first aid to Victims; and
d. report to the competent authorities if Violence against Victims occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 15

1. The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision over the implementation of MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes providing implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of services for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BADUNG REGENCY

NUMBER 15 YEAR 2013 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 8

1. Community Institutions may establish an IPU.
2. The establishment of an IPU as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be guided by the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 17

In the event that the IPU as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (1) has not been established, the existing P2TP2A shall continue to carry out the duties and functions of integrated services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.

CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 14

Funding for the provision of Protection for Women and Children from acts of Violence shall be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 8

Paragraph (1)
What is meant by "community institutions" are institutions formed by members of Indonesian citizen society voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations.

Paragraph (2)
Sufficiently clear.

CHAPTER VIII

REPORTING

Article 13

1. The Regent is responsible for preparing a report on the implementation of MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region to the Governor with a copy submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.
2. The reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.

Article 12

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.
3. The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb.

9. CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a Woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences suffering and/or hardship as a result of Violence and/or threat of Violence.
12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can perform their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.

15. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence from the Region to their Region of origin.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a Woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences suffering and/or hardship as a result of Violence and/or threat of Violence.
12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can perform their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
14. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally.
15. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence from the Region to their Region of origin.
16. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
17. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or Victims of acts of Violence.
18. 19. COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 16

a. establish family partners at the sub-district/village level by the community;
b. conduct independent socialization of the rights of Women and Children;
c. provide first aid to Victims; and
d. report to the competent authorities if Violence against Victims occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Child Victims of Violence aims to:
a. prevent all forms of Violence against Women and Children;
b. protect Women and provide services to Women and Child Victims of Violence; and
c. empower Women and Child Victims of Violence.

FUNDING

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 11

Article 12

2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.
3. The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 16

d. report to the competent authorities if Violence against Victims occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Child Victims of Violence aims to:
a. prevent all forms of Violence against Women and Children;
b. protect Women and provide services to Women and Child Victims of Violence; and
c. empower Women and Child Victims of Violence.

Article 12

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.

3. The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 11

1. To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
2. The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
3. Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Work Units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.
4. Monitoring shall be conducted from the planning stage to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence for the current year.

CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 14

Funding for the provision of Protection for Women and Children from acts of Violence shall be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 15

1. The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision over the implementation of MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes providing implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of services for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 14

Funding for the provision of Protection for Women and Children from acts of Violence shall be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 12

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.
3. The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, Violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for Victims of Violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Badung Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children Victims of Violence particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Badung Regency.

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 11

1. To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
2. The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
3. Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Work Units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.
4. Monitoring shall be conducted from the planning stage to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence for the current year.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Badung Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Badung.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Badung Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a Woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences suffering and/or hardship as a result of Violence and/or threat of Violence.
12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can perform their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
14. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally.
15. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence from the Region to their Region of origin.
16. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
17. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or Victims of acts of Violence.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and Child Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and Legal Aid.
19. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.

Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences suffering and/or hardship as a result of Violence and/or threat of Violence.
12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can perform their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
14. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally.
15. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence from the Region to their Region of origin.
16. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
17. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or Victims of acts of Violence.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and Child Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and Legal Aid.
19. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.
